summary: Jacqueline I. Stone specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied at San Francisco State University and UCLA under doctoral supervisor William R. LaFleur. She was a professor at Princeton University (1990–2019) and served as president of the Society for the Study of Japanese Religions (~1996–1998).

Jacqueline Suthren Hirst is a scholar in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who completed her doctoral studies under Julius Lipner. Her career includes posts at the University of Manchester, where she was attested in 2005 and served as an Honorary Research Fellow in 2026.

Jacques André was a linguist and historian who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris under Jules Marouzeau. He held academic posts at Aix-Marseille University (1947–1953), École Pratique des Hautes Études (1953–1978), and Paris Nanterre University (1965–1970).

Jacques Bacot worked in Tibetology and linguistics after studying at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot. He held posts at the EPHE (1919–1938), the University of Paris (~1936–1958), and served as president of the Société Asiatique (1945–1954).

Jacques David Ehni was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Evangelische Seminare Maulbronn und Blaubeuren and the University of Tübingen (Dr.Theol.). His teaching career included posts at the Lyceum of Ludwigsburg and Humboldt-Gymnasium Ulm.

Jacques Gernet was a scholar of sinology, history, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Algiers, INALCO, and EPHE. He held posts at EFEO, EPHE, Paris Diderot University, and the Collège de France (1975–1992).

Jacques Giès worked in sinology, art history, and Buddhist studies, studying under Flora Blanchon and earning a doctorate from Paris-Sorbonne University. He taught at Paris-Sorbonne (1974–1998) and École du Louvre (1998–2008), and served as curator and president (2008–2011) at the Guimet Museum.

Jacques Leider is a historian and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at INALCO, Paris-Sorbonne University, and the University of Luxembourg, completing his doctorate under Denise Bernot. He taught at Chulalongkorn University (1995–1999) and was appointed Maître de conférences at the EFEO in 2001.

Jacques Maritain was a philosopher who studied at Lycée Henri-IV, the Faculty of Arts of Paris under Henri Bergson, and the University of Notre Dame. He later held an academic post at the University of Chicago.

Jacques May specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, completing his doctorate under Constantin Régamey. He served as editor-in-chief of Hōbōgirin (~1968–1981) and as professor at the University of Lausanne (~1977–1992).

Jacques Scheuer was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Université catholique de Louvain and Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Madeleine Biardeau. He served as professor at Université catholique de Louvain (~1978–2007) and held a post at Centre Sèvres.

Jacques van Ginneken was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University under Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck. He held posts as professor at the Catholic University of America in 1923 and at Radboud University Nijmegen from 1923 to 1945.

Jacques-Albert Cuttat was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology who studied at the Universities of Bern and Paris. He served as PD of Commercial Law at the University of Bern (1935) and later taught at Columbia University and the Sorbonne.

Jadunath Sarkar was a historian who studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta. He held teaching posts at Patna College (1899–1926) and Banaras Hindu University (1917–1919), and served as vice-chancellor of the University of Calcutta (1926–1928).
Jae-gwon Kim is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at Ryukoku University in 2007 and held a post at the same institution.

Jagaddhar Zadoo was an Indologist whose career included serving at the Research and Archaeological Department of Jammu and Kashmir, where he was attested from 1924 to 1930 and as Superintendent in 1947.

Jagadish Chandra Chatterji was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who earned a B.A. at the University of Cambridge. In 1911, he served as Director of the Research and Archaeological Department of Jammu and Kashmir.

Jagannath Upadhyaya was an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He was a professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1980–1983) and became the first director of the Rare Buddhist Text Research Project at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies in 1985.

Jagdish Kashyap studied at Patna College, BHU, and Vidyalankara Pirivena under Rahul Sankrityayan. A scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics, he was professor at Banaras Hindu University (~1940–1951) and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1959–1965), and director of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1951–1973).

Jaideva Singh worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, studying under Srikrishna Harihirlekar, Nankoo Bhaya Telang, and Swami Lakshman Joo. He was chief producer at All India Radio (~1956–1962) and chairman of the Uttar Pradesh Sangeet Natak Akademi (1973).
